biography.plain_text: Michael Bradfield is a British entrepreneur who founded Hospital Plan Insurance Services, a direct seller of health, accident and life cover. A law graduate of the London School of Economics, he built a career in insurance and direct marketing. The business was sold to AIG in 2000; he remained chief executive until 2006.

long_biography.plain_text:
Mobile and modular scanners were central to Michael Bradfield’s work as chairman of Fairford Medical. The company supplied MRI and CT equipment to healthcare providers, adding diagnostic capacity for NHS trusts and private hospitals. In 2025, Medneo acquired its scanner fleet, taking that equipment into a larger diagnostic services network.

Bradfield also backed the development of proton therapy, which uses beams of protons to treat cancer. Through his investment company Fairford Capital, he provided Advanced Oncotherapy with a £2 million loan in 2015. The financing supported production of its first LIGHT accelerator. He had also bought shares in the company, combining equity investment with lending to support its development programme.
